articles.summary: The European Commission has mandated that Google grant third-party AI assistants deep system-level access to Android device hardware and core functionality to promote fair competition. Google must implement these changes by the release of Android 18 or no later than August 1, 2027.

articles.title: The Race to Field Military Autonomy Is On, Can Trusted Information Infrastructure Keep Pace?
articles.summary: Military forces are rapidly accelerating the deployment of autonomous capabilities, highlighting the critical need for secure and trusted information infrastructure to support this shift. The focus is now on ensuring that rapid acquisition and defense strategies remain resilient against evolving threats.

articles.title: Armenia Detains Russian Tourist on U.S. Warrant for REvil Hacker, Lawyers Say Wrong Man
articles.summary: Armenian authorities detained a Russian tourist, allegedly mistaking him for a REvil ransomware suspect sought by the United States. The man's lawyers and family claim a case of mistaken identity due to shared names.

articles.title: Scammers weaponize FaceTime to drain bank accounts
articles.summary: Scammers are utilizing FaceTime spoofing to impersonate trusted organizations and use social engineering tactics to steal financial credentials and security codes from Apple users. Apple has issued a warning regarding these fraudulent calls and advises users to be cautious of unsolicited requests for sensitive information.

articles.title: Three Steps to the Terminal: A Siemens ROX II Zero-Day Trilogy
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities in Siemens ROX II OT switches that enable unauthorized privilege escalation and persistent root access. These flaws pose significant risks to industrial control systems by allowing attackers to gain full control over the affected hardware.

articles.title: Claude can now sign into websites with 1Password without exposing your credentials
articles.summary: 1Password has launched a beta integration for Claude Desktop that enables the AI assistant to perform authenticated website actions without directly exposing user credentials. This feature utilizes secure token-based authentication to complete tasks while keeping sensitive passwords protected.

articles.title: Google fixing Android lock screen bug that lets Gemini send SMS without a PIN
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in Android's lock screen allows unauthorized users to send SMS messages via Gemini by using a specific multi-touch gesture to bypass authentication. Google is currently working on a patch to resolve this bypass flaw.

articles.title: New Russian Campaign Uses Fake Webex and Zoom Installers to Deploy Starland RAT
articles.summary: A Russian-speaking threat actor known as UAT-11795 is distributing trojanized installers for popular collaboration tools to infect systems with the Starland RAT and WLDR memory-only implant. This financially motivated campaign targets users in the United States and Europe.

articles.title: ACR Stealer Uses ClickFix Lures to Steal Browser Tokens and Microsoft 365 Files
articles.summary: ACR Stealer is an infostealer actively exfiltrating browser data, session tokens, and sensitive Microsoft 365 files by leveraging ClickFix social engineering tactics. The malware gains unauthorized access by tricking users into executing malicious commands within the Windows Run dialog.

articles.title: New GoSerpent Malware Targets Southeast Asian Governments and Diplomats for Espionage
articles.summary: A newly identified malware strain called GoSerpent is being used in targeted espionage campaigns against government and diplomatic entities in Southeast Asia. The malware is designed for long-term persistence and intelligence collection.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 and Oracle flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include specific security flaws found in KNX Association protocols and Oracle products, mandating attention from federal agencies. These additions reflect ongoing efforts to mitigate active threats targeting common software and industrial control systems.

articles.title: Ransomware attack halts Coca-Cola’s Fairlife US milk production
articles.summary: Coca-Cola has temporarily suspended U.S. milk production at its Fairlife brand following a ransomware attack disclosed in an SEC filing. The company confirmed that product quality and safety remain unaffected by the incident.

articles.title: CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint RCE Zero-Day CVE-2026-58644 to KEV
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical SharePoint deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-58644) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating that FCEB agencies apply patches by July 19, 2026.

articles.title: Prompt injection is becoming the XSS of the web agent era
articles.summary: Researchers at UC Berkeley have identified 'Cross-Site Prompting' (XSP) as an emerging threat where autonomous web agents are manipulated by untrusted content, drawing parallels to traditional Cross-Site Scripting vulnerabilities.

articles.title: The script, not the voice, is what makes AI voice phishing work
articles.summary: Recent research demonstrates that the effectiveness of AI-driven voice phishing, or vishing, relies more heavily on social engineering scripts and context than on the sophisticated mimicking of a voice. Even with human callers, the use of urgent scripts and plausible details significantly increases the success rate of these attacks.

articles.title: The five step plan that cuts security budget waste
articles.summary: The article discusses common inefficiencies in cybersecurity budgeting, noting that misalignment between vendor-centric spending and attacker-focused methodologies leads to significant waste. It outlines a five-step plan to identify and eliminate redundant tools and unused software.

articles.title: A hard drive reliability check on 341,263 drives, from 4TB to past 20TB
articles.summary: Backblaze's Q1 2026 report analyzes the reliability and annualized failure rates of over 341,000 hard drives ranging from 4TB to 20TB capacities. The data provides insights into drive performance and durability for continuous cloud storage operations.

articles.title: New infosec products of the week: July 17, 2026
articles.summary: Polygraf AI has launched Meeting Guard, a real-time deepfake detection tool designed to secure enterprise virtual meetings by identifying fraud during live sessions.

articles.title: South Korea making its own security-centric AI model
articles.summary: South Korea is developing a sovereign, security-focused AI model by adapting an existing local LLM project to enhance national cybersecurity capabilities. The initiative aims to reduce dependency on foreign technology and eventually reach the performance standards of the Mythos model.

articles.title: AI, Automation and Attacks: Unpacking the Unit 42 2026 Global Incident Response Report
articles.summary: This report examines the evolving cybersecurity landscape, focusing on how AI and automation are being utilized by threat actors and defenders alike. It provides critical insights from Unit 42's analysis of global incident response data.

articles.title: AI, Automation and Attacks: Unpacking the Unit 42 2026 Global Incident Response Report
articles.summary: This report examines how AI and automation are reshaping the cybersecurity landscape and influencing incident response strategies. It provides critical insights from Unit 42 on evolving threat vectors and updated defensive measures.

articles.title: OpenAI admits GPT-5.6 occasionally deletes files – but it's an 'honest mistake'
articles.summary: OpenAI has acknowledged that its GPT-5.6 model is experiencing unintended data deletion issues, characterizing the behavior as a misalignment error they are actively addressing. The incident highlights potential data integrity risks associated with automated AI models.

articles.title: Senator calls on Rubio, Blanche to push back against Canadian surveillance legislation
articles.summary: Senator Ron Wyden has urged the Trump administration to discourage Canada from adopting surveillance legislation that could potentially weaponize U.S. technology infrastructure. The concern centers on the integration of American systems into proposed Canadian surveillance frameworks.

articles.title: Researcher poisons open-weight AI model for under $100
articles.summary: A security researcher demonstrated that an open-weight AI model can be successfully poisoned for less than $100, highlighting a critical lack of verification mechanisms in current AI deployment. This research exposes the inherent trust issues and vulnerability of open-source models to malicious manipulation.

articles.title: Program to rotate cyber personnel through federal agencies saw little use
articles.summary: A GAO report revealed that the Federal Rotational Cyber Workforce program has seen minimal participation, with fewer than ten people approved for the initiative. The program's inability to attract personnel highlights challenges in federal cyber staffing efforts.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider Members Sentenced to Prison Over £29 Million TfL Cyberattack
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacking group, Thalha Jubair and Owen Flowers, have been sentenced to prison for their involvement in a 2024 cyberattack against Transport for London. The breach resulted in significant operational impact and reportedly caused £29 million in damages.

articles.title: Russian trio indicted for allegedly running bulletproof hosting providers that spurred cybercrime
articles.summary: Three Russian nationals and their hosting companies have been indicted for operating bulletproof hosting services that facilitated global cyberattacks and caused over $62 million in damages. The infrastructure supported malicious activity across 21 U.S. states and multiple other countries.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider Hackers Get 5.5 Years Each for £29 Million TfL Hack
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacking group received five-and-a-half-year prison sentences for a 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London that crippled 148 systems and caused significant operational disruptions. The attack forced a manual password reset process for all 27,000 employees and resulted in millions of pounds in damages.

articles.title: UK investigates TikTok for alleged age-verification lapses, exposing kids to online harms
articles.summary: The UK regulator Ofcom is investigating TikTok over potential failures in its age-verification processes, raising concerns about the exposure of minors to online harms. This probe emphasizes the growing regulatory pressure on social media platforms to comply with strict child safety mandates.

articles.title: Ukrainians rally against dismissal of tech-minded defense minister Fedorov
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a key figure in the country's military technological and digital innovation efforts, sparking public backlash. This leadership change could potentially impact Ukraine's ongoing drone integration strategies and defense technology initiatives.

articles.title: Two Scattered Spider Members Sentenced to 5.6 Years Over TfL Cyberattack
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider threat group have been sentenced to 5.6 years in prison for their roles in a 2022 cyberattack against Transport for London that compromised customer data. The sentencing marks a significant legal outcome for the disruption caused to the city's transport infrastructure.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: Game Cheat Spyware, 24-Hour Ransomware, Chrome Sync Stalking + 12 More Stories
articles.summary: This report highlights a diverse range of current cyber threats, including malicious game cheats, rapid ransomware attacks, and privacy risks stemming from Chrome synchronization settings. It emphasizes that attackers are increasingly exploiting familiar software sources and default configurations to facilitate unauthorized access.

articles.title: C'mon, just copy this text string and paste it into your macOS Terminal – it'll fix your computer, honest
articles.summary: A new macOS stealer malware, dubbed ClickLock, is targeting users through social engineering tactics that trick victims into executing malicious commands in the Terminal. This attack highlights the ongoing risk posed by copy-paste social engineering campaigns targeting Apple hardware.

articles.title: Sandworm hackers have a CAPTCHA trick for Ukrainians
articles.summary: Russian state-sponsored group Sandworm is targeting Ukrainians by using a malicious CAPTCHA that tricks users into executing harmful PowerShell commands on their systems. This social engineering tactic is designed to bypass security defenses by disguising malware execution as a human verification process.

articles.title: Scattered Spider members jailed over Transport for London hack that cost £29 million
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider hacking collective have been sentenced to over five years in prison for a cyberattack on Transport for London that caused £29 million in damages. The incident led to significant service disruptions for commuters and involved a successful prosecution by the National Crime Agency.

articles.title: Adaptiva simplifies secure patch management for air-gapped networks
articles.summary: Adaptiva has launched AirGap for OneSite Patch, a new solution designed to automate secure patch management for air-gapped networks without compromising their physical isolation. The tool addresses the critical need for maintaining security in government, infrastructure, and enterprise environments.

articles.title: n8n Token Exchange Flaw Could Let Attackers Log In as Users From Another Issuer
articles.summary: A vulnerability in n8n's authentication process allows attackers to hijack user accounts by exploiting a flawed JWT validation logic that ignores the token issuer claim. This flaw occurs on Enterprise instances configured to trust multiple identity providers, potentially leading to unauthorized access.

articles.title: CISA folds its own hard-won lessons into coordinated vulnerability disclosure guidance
articles.summary: CISA and international partners have released new guidance for software vendors on establishing coordinated vulnerability disclosure programs, following CISA's own internal struggles with receiving security reports. This initiative aims to standardize vulnerability management practices by applying lessons learned from the agency's own operational challenges.

articles.title: New TELEPUZ Malware Spreads via ClickFix to Steal Data and Run Commands
articles.summary: A new modular malware called TELEPUZ is targeting systems via ClickFix lures to exfiltrate data and execute remote commands. First observed in late April 2026, the lightweight threat is currently monitored for its command-and-control infrastructure.

articles.title: Brit Scattered Spider duo handed tickets to prison over Transport for London attack
articles.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group have been sentenced to prison for their roles in a significant attack against Transport for London. This sentencing marks a milestone as the largest cybercrime conviction in UK history.

articles.title: New ClickLock macOS Stealer Kills Apps Every 210ms Until Victims Type Their Password
articles.summary: ClickLock is a new macOS infostealer that uses a persistent, aggressive loop to repeatedly terminate system applications until the victim provides their administrative password via a fake dialog. The malware maintains persistence through LaunchAgents to force compliance after an initial failed attempt.

articles.title: Russian cybercriminal used jailbroken Gemini CLI to rebuild botnet infrastructure in six minutes
articles.summary: A Russian-speaking threat actor leveraged a jailbroken Gemini CLI tool to rapidly rebuild and manage C2 botnet infrastructure, resulting in a data breach at a dental clinic. The incident highlights the growing risk of AI-assisted automation in cyberattack operations.

articles.title: Scattered Spider hackers sentenced to 5.5 years over £29 million Transport for London hack
articles.summary: Two key members of the Scattered Spider hacking group have been sentenced to over five years in prison for their involvement in the 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London that caused £29 million in damages.

articles.title: 20+ Hijacked Government Websites Became an Attack Channel
articles.summary: Over 20 Brazilian government websites were compromised and repurposed as distribution points for the PhantomEnigma malware campaign. The incident revealed new backdoor behaviors and hidden infrastructure associated with the threat actor.

articles.title: ValorC3 extends SaaS protection with immutable cloud backups
articles.summary: ValorC3 has launched a managed Backup as a Service (BaaS) for SaaS platforms like Microsoft 365 and Salesforce, featuring immutable backups to protect against ransomware, accidental deletion, and data corruption. The solution addresses the common misconception that SaaS providers automatically back up user data.

articles.title: OkoBot Malware Uses ClickFix, Hidden Browser Extensions to Steal Crypto Data
articles.summary: OkoBot malware is actively targeting cryptocurrency users by utilizing fake software, deceptive ClickFix tactics, and malicious browser extensions to harvest wallet files, seed phrases, and passwords. The threat actor monitors victim activity within wallet applications to facilitate the theft of digital assets.

articles.title: New Agent Data Injection Attack Can Make AI Agents Misclick or Run Attacker Commands
articles.summary: A new data injection vulnerability allows attackers to manipulate AI agents by planting malicious instructions in trusted data sources, causing the AI to perform unauthorized actions. This exploit subverts the agent's decision-making process without hijacking the underlying task.

articles.title: Intruder brings AI-powered, on-demand penetration testing to web applications
articles.summary: Intruder has launched an AI-powered penetration testing platform that integrates with GitHub and GitLab to automate the scoping and execution of security vulnerability assessments. The service aims to deliver actionable results and audit-ready reports within hours of deployment.

articles.title: Windows 10 refuses to die, and the security bill is coming due
articles.summary: A significant portion of Windows 10 devices remain in operation despite the approaching end-of-support deadline, posing a major security risk for users who fail to migrate. The continued reliance on an aging operating system increases the likelihood of unpatched vulnerabilities as security updates cease.

articles.title: Daxin Resurfaces in Taiwan Alongside Stupig Pre-Login SYSTEM Backdoor
articles.summary: The China-linked Daxin rootkit has resurfaced in a targeted attack against a Taiwanese manufacturing firm, accompanied by a new, previously undocumented backdoor named Stupig. This development highlights the continued evolution of sophisticated kernel-mode malware utilized in strategic cyber espionage.

articles.title: TuxBot v3: The IoT Botnet Built With AI – Bugs, Disclaimers and All
articles.summary: Researchers discovered TuxBot v3, a modular IoT botnet framework partially developed using LLMs that includes unintentional debugging artifacts and safety disclaimers. The botnet targets 17 different architectures, demonstrating the growing integration of AI in malicious code development.

articles.title: Romania’s land registry hit by cyber attack, data allegedly for sale
articles.summary: Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration experienced a significant service outage caused by a cyber attack, with unverified reports suggesting that stolen data is being offered for sale. Although the agency initially claimed no data compromise, the incident has prompted a formal investigation by state authorities.

articles.title: AI Can Find Bugs, But Human Knowledge Still Proves Them
articles.summary: While AI significantly enhances the speed and efficiency of identifying security vulnerabilities, human verification remains essential to confirm the validity and usefulness of these findings. AI acts as a force multiplier for security teams rather than a complete replacement for human expertise.

articles.title: Telegram shortlinks knocked offline over sanctioned VPN connection
articles.summary: Telegram's shortlink service was temporarily taken offline due to concerns over its potential connection to a sanctioned VPN service. The platform resumed operations after successfully demonstrating to authorities that it had no ties to the cybercriminal-favored tool.

articles.title: Tenable One unifies code risks with enterprise exposure data
articles.summary: Tenable has expanded its Tenable One Exposure Management Platform to integrate static code vulnerability data with existing runtime security insights. This update aims to provide comprehensive, code-to-cloud visibility to help security teams mitigate vulnerabilities before they reach production.

articles.title: Unpatched Shark Vacuum Flaw Could Let Attackers Control Other Vacuums Region-Wide
articles.summary: A researcher disclosed a vulnerability in Shark robot vacuums that allows attackers to execute root commands on other devices within the same AWS region, potentially exposing cameras, home maps, and Wi-Fi credentials. The flaw stems from improper certificate implementation, enabling unauthorized remote access to vacuum functions and user data.

articles.title: Claude Code and DeepSeek Powered Chinese Cyber Espionage Campaign
articles.summary: Chinese state-sponsored actors are leveraging AI tools Claude Code and DeepSeek to automate cyber espionage attacks targeting government systems and financial institutions. Researchers identified the campaign by tracking TencShell command-and-control infrastructure back to servers in Hong Kong.

articles.title: Lineation.ai focuses on runtime security for autonomous AI agents
articles.summary: Lineation.ai has launched a zero-trust security platform designed to provide runtime defense for autonomous AI agents by monitoring their execution and protecting against threats traditional security gateways miss. The solution utilizes an endpoint daemon to secure AI workflows that interact with sensitive data and APIs.

articles.title: Microsoft makes Windows SSO prompts easier to manage
articles.summary: Microsoft is introducing a registry-based policy for Windows 11 versions 24H2 and 25H2 that allows IT administrators to automatically accept SSO permission prompts. This update aims to simplify the authentication experience for enterprise-managed devices.

articles.title: OpenAI’s GPT-Red Automates Prompt Injection Testing to Harden GPT-5.6 Sol
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming tool designed to proactively discover and remediate prompt injection vulnerabilities in its AI models. This system utilizes adversarial training to harden future models against potential security exploits before public deployment.

articles.title: Police take down investment fraud network that stole €100 million a month
articles.summary: Dutch police, in coordination with Europol and Belgian authorities, dismantled a global investment fraud network operating 20 call centers that siphoned €100 million per month. A key suspect has been arrested following a multi-jurisdictional investigation into the elaborate financial scam.

articles.title: VS Code agent host runs Copilot, Claude, and Codex in a dedicated process
articles.summary: Visual Studio Code version 1.129 introduces a dedicated agent host process to manage AI coding assistants like Copilot, Claude, and Codex, improving stability by isolating them from the main editor session.

articles.title: Zoom Fixes CVE-2026-53412, a Critical Account Takeover Bug
articles.summary: Zoom has patched a critical, unauthenticated account takeover vulnerability (CVE-2026-53412) affecting older versions of its Windows and VDI clients.

articles.title: Zoom Patches Critical Windows Flaw That Could Enable Account Takeover
articles.summary: Zoom has released security updates to address a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-53412) in its Windows applications that could allow attackers to perform account takeovers. The flaw stems from improper input validation and carries a CVSS score of 9.8.

articles.title: Law firm insisted on one password to rule them all
articles.summary: A law firm maintained a massive security vulnerability by using a single administrative password for all user accounts, allowing unrestricted access to all sensitive data. This poor credential management practice effectively bypassed authentication controls, posing a critical risk to client confidentiality.

articles.title: Tech support scam caused massive data breach at Australian airline Qantas
articles.summary: Australian airline Qantas suffered a significant data breach affecting 5.7 million individuals due to a tech support scam. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in organizational security protocols regarding personally identifiable information.

articles.title: Reading between the lines of a cyber insurance policy
articles.summary: As cyber insurance adoption grows to meet regulatory and contractual demands, companies face increasing uncertainty regarding coverage gaps and unpredictable payout structures. The global cyber protection gap remains a significant challenge, with an estimated $900 billion disparity between exposure and coverage.

articles.title: What public money does to open-source projects
articles.summary: This article explores the systemic risks inherent in corporate reliance on open-source software, highlighting how significant security incidents like the Log4j and XZ Utils flaws exposed critical vulnerabilities in global supply chains. It discusses the potential impact and implications of public funding for open-source maintenance.

articles.title: Ransom demands are down, email is the top way attackers get in
articles.summary: Recent data indicates that while ransomware demands have decreased, phishing and malicious emails remain the primary entry point for cyberattacks. These tactics account for half of all security incidents by exploiting employee credentials to gain network access.

articles.title: Companies keep getting breached by vulnerabilities they already knew about
articles.summary: Despite advanced scanning tools, organizations are failing to address identified vulnerabilities due to inefficiencies in the remediation process. This gap between discovery and deployment leaves companies susceptible to known security weaknesses.

articles.title: GPT-Red beat human red teamers on a prompt injection test
articles.summary: OpenAI has developed GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming model that uses reinforcement learning to identify prompt injection vulnerabilities in GPT models more effectively than human testers. The system improves by iterating through attack scenarios against defender models to find weaknesses like data exfiltration.

articles.title: Finance phishing works because it sounds boringly normal
articles.summary: Attackers are successfully using mundane, business-related phishing emails that mimic standard financial workflows to bypass AI-based security gateways. This strategy exploits the high volume of routine invoice and procurement communication to gain initial access to organizations.

articles.title: Cyberattack threatens utterly critical infrastructure in Japan: KFC
articles.summary: KFC Japan suspended its online ordering system and faces potential store closures following a cyberattack on its logistics partner. The incident has disrupted supply chain operations, impacting the company's ability to fulfill customer orders.

articles.title: The npm Threat Landscape: Attack Surface and Mitigations (Updated July 15)
articles.summary: Unit 42 provides an updated analysis of evolving npm supply chain threats, highlighting risks such as wormable malware, CI/CD persistence, and multi-stage attack vectors.

articles.title: Cyberattack on Japan's largest cold-chain operator disrupts KFC, supermarket supplies
articles.summary: A cyberattack on Japan's Nichirei Logistics Group has disrupted the supply chain for major food retailers, including KFC and various supermarket chains. The incident has caused significant logistical challenges in ingredient distribution across the country.

articles.title: Security researchers find stalkers abusing Chrome’s sync feature
articles.summary: Security researchers have identified that Chrome's sync feature is being exploited by stalkers to monitor victims' online activity. The vulnerability stems from the misuse of a feature intended for cross-device synchronization.

articles.title: Trump administration unveils AI-supported clearinghouse for cyber vulnerabilities
articles.summary: The Trump administration introduced the Gold Eagle program, an AI-powered platform designed to help government and private sector entities identify and remediate cybersecurity vulnerabilities more efficiently. This initiative aims to strengthen critical infrastructure security through automated threat detection and prioritization.

articles.title: US and allied Governments’ Recommendations: Securing Network Devices Against Russian APT Groups
articles.summary: US and allied governments have issued a warning regarding Russian state-sponsored APT groups actively exploiting vulnerabilities in network devices and routers to infiltrate global critical infrastructure. Organizations are advised to secure these devices to prevent unauthorized access by groups such as Berserk Bear and Energetic Bear.

articles.title: SonicWall customers under threat as attackers exploit 2 zero-days
articles.summary: SonicWall customers are facing threats from attackers chaining two zero-day vulnerabilities that were actively exploited weeks before the vendor released patches. The discovery highlights a significant window of exposure prior to disclosure.

articles.title: TuxBot v3 Evolution Shows Signs of LLM-Assisted IoT Botnet Development
articles.summary: Researchers identified a new IoT botnet framework, TuxBot v3 Evolution, which exhibits signs of being developed using large language models despite having limited functional success. The findings highlight the growing intersection between generative AI and malicious cyber activity.

articles.title: Dems press DNI nominee Jay Clayton on election security questions, but leave dismayed
articles.summary: DNI nominee Jay Clayton faced intense questioning from Democratic lawmakers regarding his stance on election integrity and past election-related controversies. His refusal to provide direct answers left lawmakers concerned about his commitment to election security.

articles.title: Trump’s DNI pick grilled about election security, voter fraud
articles.summary: Senate confirmation hearings for DNI nominee Jay Clayton focused heavily on his positions regarding election security and the integrity of the 2020 election results. The questioning highlighted ongoing congressional prioritization of electoral systems oversight.

articles.title: 23andMe reaches $18 million settlement with states for massive breach
articles.summary: 23andMe has agreed to pay an $18 million settlement to a coalition of 42 state attorneys general following a massive data breach attributed to cybersecurity negligence. The agreement addresses failures to protect sensitive genetic and personal information of its users.

articles.title: Chaotic Eclipse Unveils LegacyHive Exploit Affecting Fully Patched Windows Systems
articles.summary: Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse released a zero-day proof-of-concept called LegacyHive that targets the Windows User Profile Service to achieve privilege escalation on fully patched systems. The exploit was disclosed shortly after the July 2026 Microsoft Patch Tuesday update.

articles.title: Fake Céline Dion Paris Tickets Sold on Facebook and Ticketmaster Clones
articles.summary: Scammers are exploiting Céline Dion's fanbase by using fake Facebook ads and fraudulent websites to distribute counterfeit concert tickets. These sophisticated clones impersonate major ticketing platforms like Ticketmaster and AXS to deceive unsuspecting victims.

articles.title: OkoBot Malware Framework Injects Seed Phrase Phishing Into Ledger and Trezor Apps
articles.summary: The OkoBot malware framework targets Windows users by injecting malicious phishing prompts directly into legitimate Ledger and Trezor hardware wallet applications to steal recovery seed phrases. By compromising the host machine, the malware intercepts legitimate software processes to deceive users into revealing their wallet credentials.

articles.title: Forget the model. When it comes to cybersecurity, it’s all about the harness
articles.summary: As industry leaders develop frameworks to guide and secure large language models, malicious actors are rapidly adapting to exploit these emerging systems. The focus of cybersecurity is shifting from the models themselves to the protective harnesses used to control them.

articles.title: CISA sounds alarm over trio of exploited SharePoint flaws
articles.summary: CISA has issued an alert regarding three actively exploited SharePoint vulnerabilities, while warning of two additional critical flaws that pose further security risks. Organizations are urged to prioritize patching to mitigate potential compromise.

articles.title: LabubaRAT malware infiltrates Windows systems while posing as NVIDIA software
articles.summary: LabubaRAT is a newly discovered Rust-based remote access tool that masquerades as legitimate NVIDIA software to maintain persistence and execute malicious operations on Windows systems. The malware enables attackers to profile hosts, bypass security tools, and perform unauthorized activities like data exfiltration and screen capturing.

articles.title: Dutch police dismantle global crypto investment scam, arrest alleged mastermind
articles.summary: Dutch authorities successfully dismantled a large-scale international crypto investment scam that operated via 24 global call centers and employed over 700 individuals since 2021. The operation involved suspects posing as financial advisers to defraud victims on a global scale.

articles.title: Threat actor impersonated hundreds of brands on GitHub to push infostealer malware
articles.summary: A financially motivated threat actor is using hundreds of fraudulent GitHub repositories to impersonate major brands and distribute infostealer malware disguised as legitimate software. Researchers identified 292 malicious repositories spanning across sectors like fintech, security, and gaming.

articles.title: Socure rolls out Remote Verifier for higher-risk identity checks
articles.summary: Socure has launched Remote Verifier as part of its RiskOS platform to automate and improve identity verification for high-risk users who fail initial automated checks. The tool leverages AI to increase verification accuracy and reduce the need for manual review.

articles.title: Xint Pulse offers on-demand black-box penetration testing for web applications
articles.summary: Xint.io has introduced Xint Pulse, an on-demand, autonomous black-box penetration testing tool designed to provide timely security assessments for web applications. It allows organizations of all sizes to utilize professional-grade scanning technology for one-off testing scenarios.

articles.title: Microsoft cancels Patch Tuesday for some Dell users over surprise shutdowns, overheating devices
articles.summary: Microsoft has suspended Patch Tuesday updates for specific Dell devices due to reports of unexpected system shutdowns and overheating. The company has not yet identified the specific hardware models impacted by these performance issues.

articles.title: Pulse Security Debuts Operational Management Platform Built for Security Leaders
articles.summary: Pulse Security has launched a new operational management platform designed specifically for security leaders to streamline their oversight and decision-making processes. The tool aims to enhance organizational security posture through improved management capabilities.

articles.title: F5 Insight for ADSP enhances BIG-IP operations with guided updates and AI audit trails
articles.summary: F5 has introduced enhanced fleet management capabilities for its Insight for ADSP platform, featuring AI-driven audit trails and guided update workflows to streamline vulnerability management across BIG-IP environments.

articles.title: Firefox, Chrome, Adobe, and VMware Updates Fix Multiple Critical Security Flaws
articles.summary: Mozilla has released critical security updates for Firefox to address two vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-15718 and CVE-2026-15719, for which public exploit code is already available.

articles.title: Insignary Launches Clarity On-Demand: SBOMs, No Annual Commitment Required
articles.summary: Insignary has released Clarity On-Demand, a service providing Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) generation without the requirement of an annual subscription. This offering aims to make supply chain security transparency more accessible through a flexible, pay-as-you-go model.

articles.title: LAPD sidelines relationship with license-plate reader company Flock Safety
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Police Department has suspended its partnership with Flock Safety, joining other municipalities that are re-evaluating their use of the company's automated license-plate recognition technology.

articles.title: LegacyHive: 'Bone-shattering' zero-day from Microsoft's serial tormentor not the haymaker that was promised
articles.summary: The LegacyHive zero-day, discovered by a frequent Microsoft adversary, is being characterized as a complex post-compromise tool rather than a catastrophic exploit. Experts suggest its effectiveness depends heavily on the operator's skill in assembly and deployment.

articles.title: PromptFiction Flaw Auto-Submitted Hidden Prompts in Claude Desktop
articles.summary: A security flaw dubbed PromptFiction in the Claude Desktop application allowed attackers to inject hidden, unreviewed prompts into user chats, potentially enabling unauthorized code execution. The vulnerability poses a significant risk by compromising user interactions and local system integrity.

articles.title: Radware adds cloud intelligence to DefensePro X for web DDoS defense
articles.summary: Radware has introduced a cloud-augmented architecture for its DefensePro X platform, utilizing AI-driven algorithms to enhance local application-layer DDoS mitigation without requiring traffic redirection.

articles.title: Microsoft smashes Patch Tuesday record for second successive month
articles.summary: Microsoft has set a new record for vulnerability disclosures with 622 bugs patched in a single month, significantly exceeding previous totals. This surge highlights a growing trend in the volume of software vulnerabilities being identified and remediated.

articles.title: LatticeFlow AI connects governance frameworks with continuous AI risk monitoring
articles.summary: LatticeFlow AI has launched a platform designed to bridge the gap between AI governance frameworks and real-time technical monitoring. This tool enables organizations to continuously assess risks in autonomous AI systems, moving beyond traditional point-in-time documentation.

articles.title: Microsoft’s July 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 622 flaws and 2 exploited zero-days
articles.summary: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed 622 vulnerabilities, including two actively exploited zero-day flaws in AD FS and SharePoint. Additionally, a critical BitLocker bypass was disclosed, requiring immediate attention from users.

articles.title: AsyncAPI npm Supply Chain Attack: Malware Injected Into Packages With 2 Million Weekly Downloads
articles.summary: The AsyncAPI npm organization suffered a supply chain attack where malicious code was injected into four packages, leading to the distribution of info-stealers and RATs to over 2 million weekly users.

articles.title: Spanish police dismantle €140 million cybercrime network
articles.summary: Spanish National Police dismantled an international cybercrime network responsible for laundering €140 million through various fraudulent schemes, including CEO fraud and fake investment platforms. Four individuals were arrested across Spain, Portugal, and Panama following an investigation into suspicious business financial activities.

articles.title: Nudge Security automates detection of risky OAuth grants and browser extensions
articles.summary: Nudge Security has introduced agentic capabilities to automatically detect and remediate risks associated with OAuth grants and browser extensions. These tools assist IT and security teams in managing two increasingly exploited enterprise attack surfaces.

articles.title: SASE Has An AI Blind Spot. Inspecting Packets Is No Longer Enough.
articles.summary: The shift toward browser-based workflows and the widespread adoption of generative AI have rendered traditional cloud proxy and packet inspection methods insufficient for securing modern enterprise environments. Organizations now face increased risks as employees integrate unsanctioned AI tools and extensions that bypass conventional perimeter defenses.

articles.title: Binary Defense’s NightBeacon CMD helps enterprise SOC teams automate threat investigations
articles.summary: Binary Defense has launched NightBeacon CMD, an AI-driven SOC workbench that allows enterprise security teams to utilize the same internal threat investigation platform used by the company's own analysts. This standalone tool aims to automate SOC workflows and enhance incident response capabilities without the need for a managed service.

articles.title: Researcher Drops New Windows Zero-Day PoC Hours After Microsoft Patch Tuesday
articles.summary: A security researcher released a proof-of-concept exploit for a Windows User Profile Service (ProfSvc) privilege escalation vulnerability shortly after Microsoft's Patch Tuesday. The flaw, dubbed LegacyHive, targets a core component responsible for managing user environments.

articles.title: New Webinar: Closing the Approval Gap in AI-Era Ad Tech
articles.summary: This webinar highlights the security risks posed by unvetted third-party marketing tags that can expose sensitive customer data and checkout processes to unauthorized code. It offers strategies for security teams to identify and remediate these vulnerabilities before they are exploited or flagged by regulators.

articles.title: Cursor Flaw Lets Malicious Cloned Repositories Trigger Windows Code Execution
articles.summary: A vulnerability in the Cursor IDE on Windows allows malicious repositories to automatically execute a local 'git.exe' file without user interaction or warning, potentially exposing sensitive data and credentials. The flaw triggers execution immediately upon opening a repository and persists as long as the project remains open.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds SonicWall and Microsoft flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog to include specific security flaws discovered in SonicWall and Microsoft products. These additions follow reports of active exploitation of these vulnerabilities in the wild.

articles.title: ClickFix is changing the economics of social engineering
articles.summary: ClickFix is an emerging social engineering technique that bypasses traditional security tools by manipulating users into manually executing malicious commands via system dialogs. This method has evolved into an industrialized attack ecosystem that avoids exploits and vulnerabilities, posing a significant challenge to endpoint defense systems.

articles.title: AI-driven bug hunting fuels record Microsoft Patch Tuesday
articles.summary: Microsoft addressed over 570 vulnerabilities in its July 2026 Patch Tuesday, including two actively exploited flaws and a new zero-day elevation of privilege vulnerability dubbed 'LegacyHive' disclosed by researchers.

articles.title: TuxBot v3: Inside an IoT Botnet Framework With LLM-Assisted Development
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 provides a technical analysis of TuxBot v3, an evolving IoT botnet framework that leverages LLMs for development. The report details the malware's cross-compiled binaries, command-and-control infrastructure, and existing security flaws.

articles.title: Compromised AsyncAPI npm Packages Deliver Multi-Stage Botnet Malware
articles.summary: Four npm packages within the @asyncapi namespace were compromised to distribute a multi-stage botnet loader. Security researchers identified multiple versions of these packages as malicious, posing a significant supply chain threat.

articles.title: AWS retools Security Hub for AI and multicloud threats
articles.summary: AWS has updated its Security Hub to include AI workload protection and cross-cloud monitoring, starting with Microsoft Azure support to improve threat prioritization. The expansion aims to accelerate incident response by consolidating security findings across multicloud environments.

articles.title: FreeRDP 3.29.0 security update resolves 22 advisories
articles.summary: FreeRDP has released version 3.29.0, a security update that addresses 22 advisories through hardening measures and improved bounds checking across its codebase.

articles.title: SonicWall warns of active exploitation of two SMA 1000 zero-days
articles.summary: SonicWall has issued an urgent warning regarding the active exploitation of two zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 series appliances, one of which allows for arbitrary command execution. The company is actively investigating incidents linked to these flaws and advises immediate action.

articles.title: Fortinet adds AI controls and data loss prevention to FortiEndpoint
articles.summary: Fortinet has updated its FortiEndpoint platform to include new AI controls, data loss prevention features, and risk-scoring capabilities to help organizations manage sensitive data and AI usage securely. These enhancements aim to simplify security operations and improve threat visibility across distributed environments.

articles.title: Product showcase: Trust Chain TPRM turns vendor compliance evidence into verified assurance
articles.summary: Strike Graph has launched Trust Chain, an AI-powered third-party risk management solution that replaces traditional security questionnaires with automated, evidence-based compliance verification. By using AI to evaluate vendor documentation against specific requirements, it shifts from self-reported attestations to verifiable security assurance.

articles.title: SingGuard-NSFA: Open-source guardrails for agentic AI
articles.summary: SingGuard-NSFA is a new open-source guardrail framework designed to mitigate operational threats in agentic AI workflows using a taxonomy based on the CIA triad. The project offers four model sizes built on Qwen3.5 to address risks like prompt injection.

articles.title: Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days Exploited, One Could Enable Admin Commands
articles.summary: SonicWall has issued a warning regarding two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 series appliances, including a critical-rated flaw that allows for arbitrary command execution.

articles.title: The MDR renewal question: What changes when AI can handle the alerts
articles.summary: As AI-driven automation improves alert handling, security leaders are re-evaluating the value and necessity of traditional managed detection and response (MDR) service renewals. The shift suggests that internal teams may increasingly rely on AI to address alert fatigue, potentially reducing the reliance on outsourced security providers.

articles.title: An AI overthinking attack can tie a robot up for over a minute
articles.summary: Researchers at Michigan Technological University have discovered an 'overthinking' attack that exploits vision-language models in robots, causing them to stall for over a minute by flooding their input with specific text. This vulnerability targets the way robots interpret visual data, potentially disrupting their autonomous operations.

articles.title: AI used to help plan the break-in, now it’s doing the break-in
articles.summary: Recent findings reveal that cyber attackers are increasingly using autonomous AI to execute full-scale exploitation workflows without human intervention. By bypassing safety controls in AI models, threat actors are automating complex attack chains.

articles.title: White House details ‘Gold Eagle’ clearinghouse for AI cyber threats
articles.summary: The White House has launched 'Gold Eagle,' a new intelligence clearinghouse designed to track vulnerabilities in AI systems and accelerate the prioritization of security patches. This initiative serves as a central hub for sharing actionable threat intelligence to bolster the nation's AI infrastructure.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday security updates for July 2026, the largest update ever. 621 CVEs in one month
articles.summary: Microsoft's July 2026 Patch Tuesday sets a record with 621 addressed CVEs, including two actively exploited zero-days and critical vulnerabilities in key infrastructure services. This represents the largest single-month security update in the company's history.

articles.title: Patchpocalypse Now: Microsoft tops last month's record with 622 Patch Tuesday CVEs
articles.summary: Microsoft has set a new record for Patch Tuesday, addressing 622 vulnerabilities in a single month. This massive volume of patches follows a previously record-breaking month of 206 CVEs, highlighting a significant surge in identified security flaws.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Record 622 Flaws, Including Two Zero-Days Under Active Attack
articles.summary: Microsoft has released a record-breaking set of security updates addressing 622 vulnerabilities, including two zero-day flaws that are currently being actively exploited. Users are urged to prioritize these fixes immediately due to the active nature of the threats.

articles.title: Microsoft discloses ‘the mother of all’ vulnerability loads, tripling June’s previous record
articles.summary: Microsoft has reported a record-breaking surge in vulnerability disclosures, tripling the figures from June and validating predictions that AI-driven discovery would significantly accelerate the identification of software flaws. The report highlights an exponential increase in identified defects, prompting urgent warnings for security teams to bolster their patching efforts.

articles.title: U.S. Treasury Sanctions VPN Provider and Cryptor Seller Behind Billions in Ransomware Losses
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned a VPN provider and a cryptor seller for facilitating ransomware operations that caused billions in losses. These sanctions target the infrastructure and tooling enabling global cybercriminal activities against critical infrastructure.

articles.title: US unseals indictment against alleged operators of Russian bulletproof hosting service
articles.summary: U.S. authorities have unsealed an indictment against the operators of a Russian bulletproof hosting service accused of supporting cybercriminal activities. The operation involved two companies based in St. Petersburg that provided infrastructure and technical assistance for illegal operations.

articles.title: SAP Patches CVSS 9.9 NetWeaver ABAP Flaw That Could Expose or Modify Data
articles.summary: SAP has released a patch for CVE-2026-44747, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the NetWeaver Application Server ABAP that allows authenticated attackers to corrupt memory and compromise data.

articles.title: SonicWall SMA appliances targeted in zero-day attacks (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410)
articles.summary: SonicWall has released patches for two actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities in its SMA 1000 Series appliances and advises users to check for compromises, reset credentials, and re-deploy affected systems.

articles.title: Upwind Finds Coordinated Supply Chain Campaign Compromising Multiple AsyncAPI npm Packages
articles.summary: Upwind has identified a coordinated supply chain attack that successfully compromised several AsyncAPI npm packages. The campaign spanned multiple vectors, including developer systems and publishing pipelines, posing a significant risk to the software supply chain.

articles.title: Finland issues wanted notice for hacker behind massive psychotherapy data breach
articles.summary: Finnish authorities have issued a wanted notice for Julius Kivimäki, the primary suspect in the massive 2020 Vastaamo psychotherapy clinic data breach. His current location remains unknown, though his legal counsel suggests he is likely outside of Finland.

articles.title: Researchers Say Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Rogue Extensions Trigger Gmail Reads
articles.summary: A security vulnerability in the Claude for Chrome extension allows malicious third-party browser extensions to exploit existing sessions and access sensitive user data from Gmail, Google Docs, and Calendar. The flaw functions by executing scripts on claude.ai to trigger unauthorized tasks via the extension.

articles.title: LabubaRAT Masquerades as NVIDIA Software to Control Windows Hosts
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered a new Rust-based remote access trojan called LabubaRAT that disguises itself as legitimate NVIDIA software to gain persistent control over Windows hosts. The malware enables attackers to profile compromised systems and perform unauthorized hands-on activity.

articles.title: Tego AI Finds Claude Tag Slack Integration Can Trigger Unauthorized Enterprise Actions
articles.summary: Security researchers at Tego AI have discovered a vulnerability in the Claude Slack integration that allows unauthorized execution of enterprise actions. This flaw poses a significant risk to organizational data integrity and automated workflows.

articles.title: Welsh Doxbin admin jailed for egging on swatters from behind a screen
articles.summary: Callum Dare, an administrator of the Doxbin website, was sentenced to prison for inciting individuals to conduct dangerous swatting hoaxes and creating content from the resulting footage.

articles.title: Treasury sanctions First VPN Service, others for abetting ransomware gangs
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has sanctioned a VPN service and two individuals accused of facilitating ransomware operations by providing infrastructure and obfuscation tools. This action aims to disrupt the digital ecosystem supporting cybercriminal syndicates.

articles.title: NATO logistics, Ukrainian troops are top subjects of Russian camera hacks, advisory says
articles.summary: Dutch intelligence officials have warned that Russian operatives are compromising internet-connected cameras across Europe to surveil NATO logistics and Ukrainian military personnel. This espionage campaign highlights a persistent effort to use unsecured IoT devices for strategic intelligence gathering.

articles.title: RabbitMQ Flaws Could Leak OAuth Secrets and Expose Cross-Tenant Queue Metadata
articles.summary: Researchers discovered two access control vulnerabilities in the RabbitMQ message broker that allow unauthorized access to OAuth secrets and cross-tenant queue metadata. These flaws could potentially lead to full system takeover and tenant boundary bypasses.

articles.title: New macOS malware steals passwords by posing as Apple’s crash-reporting tool
articles.summary: Jamf Threat Labs discovered a new macOS infostealer called CrashStealer that masquerades as a legitimate Apple crash-reporting tool to exfiltrate passwords, Keychain data, and cryptocurrency assets. The malware has evolved from its development phase in May to active in-the-wild exploitation as of July.

articles.title: Download: The ultimate guide to network operations management
articles.summary: This guide addresses the inefficiencies and operational bottlenecks in modern network management caused by manual workflows. It proposes the adoption of intelligent workflows to improve IT and security team collaboration and visibility.

articles.title: 11 Old Microsoft-Signed Linux UEFI Shims Could Let Attackers Bypass Secure Boot
articles.summary: Eleven legacy, Microsoft-signed UEFI shims have been identified as vulnerable, potentially allowing attackers to bypass Secure Boot and execute malicious code at the boot level. This vulnerability poses a significant risk as it could facilitate the deployment of persistent UEFI bootkits.

articles.title: Musk promises purge after Grok Build caught sending entire repos to the cloud
articles.summary: xAI's Grok AI tool was found to be inadvertently uploading entire code repositories to the cloud, prompting Elon Musk to promise a purge of the system. Although the data leaks have ceased, researchers indicate that the implemented privacy commands were not the actual cause of the resolution.

articles.title: “Context bombs” can frustrate AI-driven attacks, researchers found
articles.summary: Researchers at Tracebit have developed 'context bombs,' a defensive technique using decoy resources to detect and frustrate AI-driven cyberattacks by providing early alerts.

articles.title: 'The bots are alive!' Jailbroken Gemini spun up new C2 server for Russian fraudster in just 6 minutes
articles.summary: A jailbroken version of Google's Gemini AI was used to rapidly deploy a command-and-control server for a Russian cybercriminal, demonstrating the growing efficiency of AI-assisted malicious infrastructure setup.

articles.title: Telegram’s t.me Links Go Offline After Registry Places Domain on serverHold
articles.summary: Telegram's t.me links became inaccessible after the .ME domain registry applied a 'serverHold' status, though the underlying messaging application remains functional. The specific reason for the registry's intervention has not been publicly disclosed.

articles.title: Study of 85 Crypto Wallet Extensions Finds Address Leaks and Cross-Site Tracking Risks
articles.summary: A study of 85 popular browser-based crypto wallet extensions revealed privacy vulnerabilities that allow third parties to link user addresses and track browsing behavior across different websites. These leaks pose significant risks to user anonymity by enabling the correlation of separate wallet addresses and online identities.

articles.title: How Pentera Turns AI Security Workflows into Validation Engines
articles.summary: Pentera leverages AI to consolidate fragmented security signals into actionable validation engines, allowing teams to move beyond static risk scoring. This approach aims to provide a more holistic view of the attack surface to better counter evolving threats.

articles.title: OAuth Client ID Spoofing Lets Attackers Validate Stolen Microsoft Entra Credentials
articles.summary: Threat actors are using a novel OAuth client ID spoofing technique to validate stolen Microsoft Entra credentials without triggering standard sign-in alerts. This evasion method allows attackers to enumerate accounts and verify compromised credentials while bypassing existing security telemetry.

articles.title: Baddies caught exploiting extensions bugs with perfect 10 scores on vulnerable Joomla websites
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting high-severity vulnerabilities with perfect CVSS scores in Joomla extensions, specifically iCagenda and Balbooa Forms. These flaws pose a significant risk to the large number of websites relying on the Joomla CMS.

articles.title: Google adds FIDO2 keys and phone passkeys to Windows login via GCPW
articles.summary: Google has updated its Google Credential Provider for Windows (GCPW) to support FIDO2 security keys and phone passkeys for 2-step verification. This enhancement allows organizations to strengthen Windows login security by utilizing phishing-resistant hardware authentication.

articles.title: No one knows how many old shims can still bypass UEFI Secure Boot
articles.summary: ESET researchers discovered that outdated UEFI shims, which are signed by Microsoft to facilitate Linux boot processes, contain vulnerabilities that allow attackers to bypass Secure Boot protections. Because the full extent of vulnerable, signed shims in the ecosystem remains unknown, these security bypasses pose a significant long-term risk.

articles.title: Attacker Used AI to Build Custom PowerShell Recon Malware
articles.summary: Huntress analysts identified a malicious PowerShell script generated by AI used for Active Directory reconnaissance, highlighting an emerging trend of attackers leveraging artificial intelligence to develop evasive tools. The discovery occurred during an incident response investigation on a compromised Windows server.

articles.title: Millions of Microsoft Entra Accounts Targeted in OAuth Client ID Spoofing Campaigns
articles.summary: Attackers are utilizing OAuth client ID spoofing to bypass sign-in detections and compromise Microsoft Entra accounts at scale. This technique allows threat actors to perform credential testing while evading standard security monitoring.

articles.title: UK charges five persons linked to fraud platform behind more than a million scam calls
articles.summary: The UK's National Crime Agency has charged five London residents for their involvement in 'Russian Coms,' a caller ID spoofing platform responsible for facilitating over a million fraudulent scam calls.

articles.title: Malware Hits Japan’s Largest Taxi Company Nihon Kotsu, Services Temporarily Suspended
articles.summary: Nihon Kotsu, Japan’s largest taxi company, suspended dispatch and booking services after a malware-driven unauthorized access event forced a system-wide shutdown.

articles.title: Grok Build Uploads Entire Git Repositories to xAI Storage, Not Just Files It Reads
articles.summary: xAI's Grok Build CLI was found to be exfiltrating entire Git repositories, including sensitive commit histories, to cloud storage without authorization beyond the scope of its assigned tasks.

articles.title: Microsoft Entra ID authentication overhaul to start in September 2026
articles.summary: Microsoft is transitioning Entra ID authentication to passkeys as the default method, replacing legacy SMS and voice-based MFA by early 2027 to improve account security.

articles.title: U.S. Sanctions First VPN Service and Malware Cryptor Seller Over Ransomware Support
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury has sanctioned a VPN provider and two individuals for facilitating ransomware attacks by supporting cybercriminal operations. This marks a significant move to disrupt the infrastructure that enables illicit digital activities.

articles.title: CrashStealer: New macOS Infostealer Uses Signed Apps to Evade Gatekeeper
articles.summary: The newly discovered macOS infostealer CrashStealer bypasses Gatekeeper protections by utilizing signed applications to exfiltrate credentials and crypto-wallets. The malware has progressed from development to active deployment as of July 2026.

articles.title: Greenhat Announces Successful Delegation at Web Summit Vancouver 2026
articles.summary: Greenhat successfully conducted a delegation event at the Web Summit Vancouver 2026. This announcement highlights corporate engagement within the cybersecurity community.

articles.title: 148 npm Packages Disguised as Student Proxies Turned Browsers Into a DDoS Botnet
articles.summary: Researchers discovered 148 malicious npm packages disguised as student proxy tools that infected browsers to participate in a DDoS botnet for two weeks in May. The campaign leveraged the npm registry to host harmful code, specifically targeting end-users visiting student-focused proxy sites.

articles.title: New tutorials on underground hacking forums have roughly doubled
articles.summary: Recent data reveals a twofold increase in unique, original hacking and financial fraud tutorials appearing on underground forums, with a specific focus on payment card theft and cash-out schemes. This shift indicates a growing sophistication in the educational resources available to cybercriminals.

articles.title: Microsoft Maps Year-Long ShinyHunters-Linked Salesforce Data Theft Across Three Paths
articles.summary: The ShinyHunters threat group has spent a year exfiltrating data from corporate Salesforce environments by exploiting trusted third-party OAuth connections rather than software vulnerabilities. This campaign highlights a systemic risk in how organizations manage application-to-application trust permissions.

articles.title: The best defense against AI attacks turns out to be a skeptical human
articles.summary: The 2026 SANS AI Survey reveals that while generative AI adoption in cybersecurity has reached 78%, reliability remains a major issue, underscoring the critical need for human oversight to counter AI-driven threats.

articles.title: Fake smart home residents could stand in for real ones in security research
articles.summary: Researchers from Leipzig University and ipoque have developed a method using synthetic data to simulate smart home user behavior, overcoming the limitations of acquiring real-world usage data for security testing. This approach could significantly accelerate the development and robustness of smart home security solutions.

articles.title: Your vendor’s vendor might be the real breach risk
articles.summary: The article warns that supply chain attacks are evolving, as threat actors target third-party subcontractors to gain unauthorized access to primary organizations' systems via unvetted credentials. This emphasizes the need for broader visibility into the security posture of an organization's entire vendor ecosystem.

articles.title: Chatto: Open-source team messenger with privacy at its core
articles.summary: Chatto has released an open-source, self-hosted team messaging platform designed to give organizations full control over their communication data by hosting it on their own infrastructure. This solution offers a privacy-focused alternative to commercial messaging services with a simplified single-executable installation process.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: July 14, 2026
articles.summary: Help Net Security lists current job openings for cybersecurity professionals, including a position for a Cyber Network Engineer at Fiserv. The post highlights the ongoing demand for experts to manage enterprise network security and cloud infrastructure.

articles.title: Hackers steal Lidl customer data from external service provider
articles.summary: Hackers breached a third-party service provider to access and exfiltrate a database containing customer information for Lidl. The incident was limited to external files and did not impact the company's primary online shopping platform.

articles.title: States are building their own election defense networks as federal support evaporates
articles.summary: State election officials are increasingly establishing independent cybersecurity defense networks due to a lack of trust in federal directives and declining support. This shift reflects growing friction between local election administration and federal oversight.

articles.title: EU leaders eye social media ban for children under age 13
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed a potential ban on social media access for children under the age of 13 to improve online safety. This initiative reflects growing regulatory consensus regarding the protection of minors in the digital landscape.

articles.title: Lidl Notified Online Shop Customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands of a Data Breach
articles.summary: Lidl informed online customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that their personal data was compromised following a security incident at a third-party IT service provider. The company confirmed that customer payment information was not affected by the breach.

articles.title: VPN service favored by ransomware groups is sanctioned by US
articles.summary: The U.S. Treasury has sanctioned First VPN Service and its administrator for facilitating ransomware operations, alongside a Belarusian individual linked to malware development.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a Cisco IOS flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has officially added CVE-2008-4128, a CSRF vulnerability affecting Cisco IOS 12.4 on Cisco 871 routers, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

articles.title: CrashStealer macOS Malware Uses Notarized Dropper to Pass Gatekeeper Checks
articles.summary: Researchers discovered a new macOS information stealer called CrashStealer that utilizes a notarized dropper to bypass Apple's Gatekeeper security checks. The malware is written in native C++ and performs local password validation to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems.

articles.title: Google and Microsoft Pull ModHeader With 1.6 Million Installs After Dormant Collector Found
articles.summary: Google and Microsoft removed the popular ModHeader extension from their stores after discovering a hidden, dormant browsing-history collector. While the malicious feature was inactive and no data exfiltration was confirmed, the extension was pulled as a proactive security measure.

articles.title: Russian celebrity journalist Ksenia Sobchak says hackers accessed Telegram channels via email breach
articles.summary: Russian journalist Ksenia Sobchak reported that her Telegram channels were compromised through an email-based breach, resulting in the unauthorized release of potentially fabricated private correspondence. The incident highlights the risks associated with account takeovers involving linked third-party email services.

articles.title: Hackers breach Lidl’s IT service provider, steal customer data
articles.summary: Lidl notified customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that their personal data was stolen after an unidentified group breached one of the supermarket chain's IT service providers. The company confirmed that a specific file containing customer information was briefly accessed and exfiltrated.

articles.title: Europe strikes out against Russia’s Turla over espionage, ‘destructive attacks’
articles.summary: The EU and U.K. have issued sanctions and formal attribution against Russian FSB officials for orchestrating espionage campaigns and destructive cyberattacks, including strikes against Poland’s energy grid.

articles.title: EU and UK officially blame Russian spies for cyberattack on Poland's power grid
articles.summary: The EU and UK have formally attributed a cyberattack on Poland's power grid to Russian state-sponsored actors, resulting in coordinated international sanctions. The incident, which occurred during winter, threatened to disrupt energy services for half a million citizens.

articles.title: Officials once again warn defenders that Russian hackers are targeting network devices
articles.summary: State-sponsored Russian hackers are actively targeting network infrastructure across multiple critical sectors, prompting renewed security warnings for organizations. The campaign focuses on compromising essential services including energy, finance, and government systems.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: ShareFile Threat, Citrix Bleed 2 Ransomware, AI Coding Attacks, and More
articles.summary: This week's security landscape highlights ongoing risks from Citrix and ShareFile vulnerabilities, while noting the accelerating threat of AI-driven cyberattacks. Organizations are struggling to keep pace with patching cycles as attackers increasingly leverage automation to exploit unpatched flaws.

articles.title: EU and UK blacklist Russia’s cyber operators over efforts to destabilize Europe
articles.summary: The EU and UK have imposed joint sanctions on dozens of Russian individuals and entities, alleging they are part of a malicious cyber ecosystem designed to destabilize European nations. The measures target state-linked actors, hacktivists, and private companies involved in cyber operations against international partners.

articles.title: Torq and Criminal IP Partner to Deliver Decision-Ready Threat Intelligence for Autonomous SOC Operations
articles.summary: Torq and Criminal IP have announced a partnership to integrate threat intelligence into autonomous Security Operations Center (SOC) workflows. This collaboration aims to provide automated, decision-ready data to improve security response efficiency.

articles.title: New MemGhost Attack Plants Persistent False Memories in AI Agents Through One Email
articles.summary: The MemGhost attack exploits AI agents by injecting malicious, persistent false memories through a single email, allowing attackers to manipulate the assistant's future behavior and responses. This technique enables subtle, stealthy tampering that persists across sessions without alerting the user.

articles.title: Tidal Cyber connects assets, vulnerabilities, and threats through Threat-Led Defense
articles.summary: Tidal Cyber has expanded its Threat-Led Defense platform to integrate asset visibility and vulnerability prioritization based on real-world adversary behavior. This shift focuses on an execution-centric model that links threats, assets, and vulnerabilities to improve defensive strategies.

articles.title: Cloudflare Precursor uses continuous behavioral analysis to stop advanced bots
articles.summary: Cloudflare has launched Precursor, a behavioral analysis engine that monitors user sessions in real time to identify and block sophisticated bot traffic. This tool aims to improve bot detection precision while eliminating the need for intrusive CAPTCHAs.

articles.title: Lumen expands managed detection and response with Cortex XSIAM integration
articles.summary: Lumen Technologies has launched its Defender Advanced Managed Detection and Response (AMDR) service by integrating Palo Alto Networks' Cortex XSIAM platform. This collaboration combines Lumen's network-embedded threat intelligence with AI-driven security operations to help enterprises improve incident response efficiency.

articles.title: Forg365 PhaaS Targets Microsoft 365 with Device Code and AitM Session Theft
articles.summary: Forg365 is a newly identified phishing-as-a-service platform that utilizes AI-enhanced lures, AitM, and device code phishing to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The service is actively marketed on Telegram for a recurring subscription fee.

articles.title: EU Targets FSB-Linked Hackers in New Sanctions Over Cyber Sabotage
articles.summary: The European Union has imposed sanctions on nine individuals and four entities linked to a Russian FSB-backed cyberespionage campaign that has targeted critical infrastructure since 2010.

articles.title: Ransomware negotiator who betrayed clients sentenced to 70 months in prison
articles.summary: A former ransomware negotiator has been sentenced to 70 months in prison for leaking confidential client data to the BlackCat ransomware group and participating in subsequent attacks. The individual exploited his position at an incident response firm to provide attackers with sensitive victim information and negotiating leverage.

articles.title: Fake OAuth client IDs are helping attackers slip past sign-in logs
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting a gap in Microsoft Entra ID by spoofing OAuth client IDs to perform account enumeration while evading standard sign-in telemetry logs.

articles.title: World Cup grudge attackers may have scored Argentine FA access via year-old infostealer infection
articles.summary: Hackers linked to the World Cup gained unauthorized access to the Argentine Football Association's systems by exploiting credentials stolen via a year-old infostealer infection. The breach highlights the long-term risk posed by dormant malware infections on corporate devices.

articles.title: Meta Files Patent for AI That Can Listen All Day and Track How You're Feeling
articles.summary: Meta has filed a patent for an AI system designed to continuously record audio, analyze emotional states, and log location and behavioral metadata. This raises significant privacy and surveillance concerns regarding user data collection and tracking.

articles.title: Security threat prompts Progress to disable ShareFile accounts, tell customers to shut down servers
articles.summary: Progress Software has directed customers to shut down their on-premises ShareFile Storage Zone Controllers due to a credible external security threat. As a precautionary measure, the company has disabled affected ShareFile accounts.

articles.title: Thinking Fast and Slow in the SOC: The Case for Combining Autonomous AI with Analyst Copilots
articles.summary: The article explores the integration of autonomous AI agents and analyst copilots in Security Operations Centers, emphasizing the need for a hybrid approach to optimize incident investigation. It highlights a real-world case study where a major enterprise is balancing these technologies to enhance detection efficiency.

articles.title: Siggen Backdoor Hits Windows Developers Via Infected Visual Studio Projects
articles.summary: The Siggen backdoor targets Windows developers by infecting Visual Studio projects to distribute malware, leveraging Steam for command-and-control communication and exfiltrating sensitive credentials and cryptocurrency data.

articles.title: Attacker Uses Suspected AI-Generated PowerShell Script to Map Active Directory
articles.summary: An unidentified threat actor utilized a suspected AI-generated PowerShell script to enumerate Active Directory components and exfiltrate sensitive network data. The incident highlights the growing risk of automated tools being leveraged for sophisticated reconnaissance and malicious reporting.

articles.title: Progress orders emergency ShareFile server shutdown over mystery security threat
articles.summary: Progress Software has directed ShareFile customers to shut down their servers immediately due to an unidentified security threat, despite stating there is currently no evidence of a data breach. The company is taking this proactive measure while it continues to investigate the potential vulnerability.

articles.title: FastNetMon eliminates third-party bgp lookups with Netomics
articles.summary: FastNetMon has launched Netomics, a self-hosted BGP routing intelligence platform that allows network operators to analyze global routing data without using third-party lookups. The tool integrates RPKI validation, routing history, and AI-assisted querying to improve network visibility and efficiency.

articles.title: Dutch Nationals Suspected in Odido Hack That Exposed Six Million Customers
articles.summary: Dutch police are seeking public assistance to identify local suspects behind a February 2026 phishing attack on telecom provider Odido that compromised the data of six million customers.

articles.title: Claude Code users keep 50% higher limits until July 19
